column1: CP - Prevent Refetch to backend and use Apollo Client Cache
column32:
*As a* customer,
*I want* the application to reuse previously loaded transaction data from the Apollo Client cache,
*so that* switching between tabs or returning to a previously viewed state is faster and avoids unnecessary requests to the backend.

h2. Description

Currently, the frontend triggers new GraphQL requests even when the required data has already been fetched during the current session. This task should leverage the Apollo Client cache to reuse existing data whenever possible, reducing redundant backend calls and improving the user experience.

The solution should ensure that cached data is displayed immediately while still allowing data to be refreshed when explicitly required.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -Previously fetched transaction data is retrieved from the Apollo Client cache when available.-
* -Unnecessary GraphQL refetches are prevented during tab navigation or when revisiting previously loaded data.-
* -The user experience remains unchanged, with data displayed correctly from the cache.-
* -Existing manual refresh or explicit refetch mechanisms continue to work as expected.-
* -No backend changes are required for this implementation.-

column1: CP - Persists the filters in transactions table
column32:
*As a* customer,
*I want* the transaction table filters to persist after reloading or sharing the page,
*so that* I don't have to reapply my filters every time I revisit or refresh the page.

h3. Acceptance Criteria

* -Applied filters are reflected in the URL as query parameters.-
* -Reloading the page preserves the active filters.-
* -Opening a URL containing filter query parameters restores the corresponding filters automatically.-
* -Updating or clearing filters updates the URL query parameters accordingly.-
* -Existing behavior for sorting, pagination, and transaction loading continues to work correctly with persisted filters.-
* -Invalid or unsupported query parameter values are ignored and default filters are applied.-

*so that* I can quickly find relevant transactions and clearly distinguish between past, current, and future activity.

* Add a new *Upcoming* transaction filter *(NEW)*.
* Integrate the *Upcoming* filter with the corresponding Forth CRM endpoint.
* Update the filter mapping and sorting logic according to the new requirements.
* Remove the *"Payments"* word from filter labels returned by the backend (if labels are provided by the API).

# All *[DESC]*
# History *[DESC]* _(Default)_
# Upcoming *[ASC]* *(NEW)*
# Monthly *[DESC]*
# Settlement *[DESC]*

*Upcoming sorting:*

* First transaction = nearest upcoming transaction.
* Last transaction = farthest future transaction.

* -The backend retrieves *Upcoming* transactions from the corresponding Forth CRM endpoint.-
* -The- *-History-* -filter remains the default filter.-

* -All remaining filters return transactions in *descending* order.-
* -Filter labels no longer include the word- *-"Payments"-*-.-
* -The backend returns filters in the required order:- *-All, History, Upcoming, Monthly, Settlement, Fees-*-.-

column1: CP - WEB - Temporarily hide email and address edit actions in profile
column32:
h2. Description

The profile page allows editing the email and home address, both of which sync with Forth. Since edits propagate directly to Forth, editing these fields overwrites the original value with no way to recover it.

Discussed with Guillermo: rather than removing the functionality, the edit actions for these two fields will be temporarily hidden (not deleted) until stakeholders (Aren, John) confirm, ahead of the upcoming production release. Password and account number editing are unaffected.

h2. Initial Findings

* Editing the email or address from the profile propagates the change to Forth.
* Once edited, the original value cannot be recovered — there is no versioning or backup of the prior value.
* Password update and account number update do not present this concern and are explicitly out of scope for this change.

!image-20260810-192710.png|width=627,alt="image-20260810-192710.png"!

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* -The email edit action is not visible in the Personal Information section.-
* -The address edit action is not visible in the Contacts section.-
* -The password update action remains visible and functional.-
* -The account number update action remains visible and functional.-
* -No underlying edit logic (handlers, modals, state) is removed — only the UI trigger is hidden, so it can be re-enabled once stakeholder confirmation is received.-

*Deliverables*

*Description:*

* Confirmed with Daniel Pardo (Supervisor): a debt can go Enrolled → Not Enrolled after being worked and dropped, keeping historical transactions from when it was enrolled.

* Verified against a real contact (debt {{393432281}}, “WFBNA CARD”, {{enrolled: "0"}} with historical settlement/fee transactions) that this scenario occurs in production.

*Decision:* Also filtered the dashboard summary totals ({{getUnitedTransactionsInfo}}) to exclude amounts linked to not-enrolled debts, matching Forth's own reporting. Implemented and validated against the real contact's data, then reverted: those transactions represent money already moved, and excluding them would make the summary inconsistent with the transaction history. column1: CP - BACK - Auth - Add per-document Terms of Service / Privacy Policy acceptance tracking
column32:
*Description*

Today, onboarding records a single yes/no flag ({{TermsAccepted}}) when the user accepts a combined "Terms" agreement — no version or date of acceptance is captured, and there's no separate acceptance for the Privacy Policy at all. Per Franklin's (company attorney) guidance relayed by Aren, both documents must be accepted individually, and it's smart to store the version and date of each acceptance.

This ticket covers the backend changes only: acceptance tracking data model and the accept endpoint. The frontend two-step read/accept UI is a separate, dependent ticket.

*Initial Findings*

* The current model has no timestamp at all — just the bare {{TermsAccepted}} boolean on {{ApplicationUser}}. No existing data needs to be migrated or reconciled.
* No mechanism exists yet to extract a document's "Last updated" date into a structured value — this needs to be built as part of this ticket.
* {{TermsAccepted}} is safe to remove entirely: confirmed it's never exposed via any API response or read by any other service, frontend, or the iOS app — it's a write-only internal flag.
* {{ApplicationUser}} is mapped in several other services' DbContexts (chats, creditors, notifications), all sharing the same physical database as auth — but a direct precedent ({{EnrolledDate}}, a prior column addition to this same entity) confirms a migration is only needed against the auth service's own context.
* This same accept endpoint is also called by iOS and Android. Requiring the new Privacy acceptance flag will break their onboarding completion until their own parity work happens — accepted as a known, temporary consequence since none of the three clients are in production yet.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* Onboarding cannot be completed unless both the Terms of Service and the Privacy Policy have been accepted.
* The exact version of each document (as actually served to the user) and the exact date/time of acceptance are recorded separately for Terms and for Privacy Policy.
* If a legal document's content is missing a valid "Last updated" marker, this is caught by automated tests before reaching a deployed environment.

column32:
*Description*

There was no dedicated place to view the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy outside of the onboarding "agreement" step — the only access point was buried inside the sign-up flow, which does not satisfy the requirement (confirmed with the company attorney) that both documents be accessible before a user downloads the app or enters any information.

This adds two public, unauthenticated routes ({{/terms}} and {{/privacy}}) that consume the backend endpoints delivered in [HED-1435|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1435], rendering the Markdown content returned by the API.

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -{{/terms}} and {{/privacy}} are accessible without an active session.-
* -Each page displays the real content returned by the backend ([HED-1435|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1435]), in the user's current language, rendered from Markdown.-
* -Cross-links inside the content (Terms → Privacy and vice versa) open in a new tab.-
* -An anonymous visitor sees a "Back to login" action; a visitor with an active session sees a "Back to dashboard" action instead.-
* -A loading state is shown while content is being fetched, and a retry option is shown if the request fails.-
* -Existing pages that share the layout component (Login, Forgot Password flow, Otp, onboarding) are unaffected.-
* -If fetching the document content fails, the page shows an error state instead of a blank screen or a broken layout.-
* -Changing the app's selected language updates the displayed content to match.-

*Decision*

Instead added a lightweight {{showBackToDashboardButton}}, mirroring the layout's existing {{showBackToLoginButton}}, which doesn't block rendering.

column1: CP - WEB - Remove component (select 2 numbers) and modify flow
column32:
*Description*

The MFA enable flow required the user to manually select a phone number (cell, home, or work) before enabling 2FA, and sent that selection to the backend.

Following [HED-1404 (backend)|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1404], {{/2fa/enable-2fa}} no longer accepts a phone number in the request — it always uses the home phone number already on file in Forth. This was discussed with the team: letting users pick or submit a different number in this flow risked overwriting the phone number on file in Forth, with no way to recover it. The phone-selection step should be removed so the flow relies entirely on the backend's automatic behavior.

!image-20260811-134759.png|width=684,alt="image-20260811-134759.png"!

*Acceptance Criteria:*

* -Enabling MFA no longer prompts the user to select a phone number.-
* -After choosing to enable MFA, the flow goes directly to the OTP verification screen.-
* -The phone number shown on the OTP screen reflects the backend's registered home phone.-
* -Editing phone numbers in the Contacts section of the profile is unaffected.-

*Initial Findings:*

* {{/2fa/enable-2fa}} ([HED-1404 (backend)|https://hiredexperts.atlassian.net/browse/HED-1404], cordoba-consumer-portal-backend#146) no longer accepts a {{phoneNumber}} body; it always uses {{user.PhoneNumber}}, which is populated from Forth's {{Phone}} field — the same field mapped to {{HomePhoneNumber}}.
* The phone-selection step ({{NewCellPhoneStep}}) was the only place in the enable-2fa modal still sending that now-unsupported body value.

*Deliverables:*

PR: [https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/222|https://github.com/cordoba-tech/cordoba-consumer-portal-frontend/pull/222|smart-link] 

Removed the phone-selection step from the MFA enable stepper and moved the {{enable-2fa}} call (now without a body) into the preceding info step, keeping its existing loading and error handling. Removed the now-unused {{phones}} prop threaded through {{MfaEnableModal}}/{{UserProfile}} and the i18n copy referencing the removed step. [^CP - Terms of Service (4.20.25)(60994211.2) (0d269ecf-9e36-40e1-b937-85fcb9e52079).doc]

column1: CP - Backend - Add Terms of Service / Privacy Policy content endpoints with language support
column32:
*Description*

The {{terms}} endpoint only served a static, language-agnostic HTML file, and no endpoint existed for Privacy Policy at all. With the approved content now available as Markdown (previous ticket), the backend needed a way to serve both documents, resolve the user's language, and fall back sensibly when a translation isn't available yet.

Updated Md legal documents:

[^PrivacyPolicy.en.md] 

[^Terms.en.md] 

*Acceptance Criteria*

* -{{GET terms}} and the new {{GET privacy}} return the approved content.-
* -Requesting a supported language (query param or {{Accept-Language}} header) returns content in that language when available.-
* -Requesting a language without an available translation (e.g., Spanish, pending approval) falls back to English rather than failing.-
* -If the required English content is ever missing, the client receives a specific, addressable error rather than a generic failure.-

*Initial Findings*

* An existing pattern for translated content in the backend solves this exact constraint by keeping cached content behind a Singleton and receiving the already-resolved language as a parameter, rather than resolving it itself.
* The {{Language}} enum's {{[Display(Name=...)]}} attributes, initially considered as a way to get human-readable names, turned out to be unused decoration nowhere read via reflection — the actual convention in use is a plain static helper class with switch-based lookups ({{LanguageHelper}}).
* Review of {{AuthController}}'s other endpoints found that every one of them dispatches through MediatR ({{Mediator.Send(new Command/Query(...))}}), including read-only queries like {{Is2FaEnabled}}/{{IsDeviceRemembered}} — the initial implementation was the only exception in the entire controller, injecting a service directly instead of going through the same dispatch pattern.

*Deliverables*
